messages.text: ask me questions so I can complete the define stage and start the build stage

Answer these to close Define and unlock the build:

1. **Launch language pair** — Which two languages at launch (Side A ↔ Side B)? Example: English ↔ Spanish. Strictly one pair, or should the pair be switchable at launch?
2. **Keyboard** — Pick one: (A) adopt **Simple Keyboard** (small, vanilla JS, inlinable into the single file — fits the "super snappy" mandate), (B) hand-roll a minimal custom keyboard (zero dependencies, total control of orientation/layout, but more build time), or (C) you want a fuller library evaluation first. Note: Mottie/Keyboard requires jQuery, which fights the single-file performance requirement.
3. **MyMemory endpoint** — Confirm you'll use the public GET endpoint already noted in the plan (`api.mymemory.translated.net/get` with `q` + `langpair` params). Do you have an email/API key to attach for higher daily quota, or is the anonymous free tier acceptable at launch?
4. **Latency target** — Is the ≤ 1 s translation round-trip confirmed? Also name the acceptable ceiling on a mid-range phone over cellular (e.g., 2 s, shown live in the in-app diagnostics panel).
5. **Optional — STT/TTS scope** — Confirm voice ships in R2 using the browser's built-in speech recognition/synthesis for the two launch languages, or defer voice to a later release and ship R2 text-only.

Short answers are fine (e.g., "1: en↔es switchable, 2: A, 3: anonymous tier, 4: 1s target / 2s ceiling, 5: ship in R2"). I'll record your answers in the plan's Define section and Decision Log, mark Define complete, and be ready to build on your next go.

this is what I was told:
b27 deployed, verified at head.

GitHub code retrieval: paste any blob or raw URL straight into the chat — https://github.com/acmeproducts/stuff/blob/main/chat.html — and the agent fetches that file's full contents into its context before working, tagged as authoritative source. Works across repos and branches (anything your PAT can read), multiple URLs per message, and the Debug log shows each fetch with its size.

Web search: a 🌐 web chip next to the engine chip toggles it per thread, persisted in GitHub. Each provider uses its own native search — Venice's enable_web_search, OpenRouter's :online routing, Anthropic's web_search tool — so no extra key or service. The agent is told it can look up docs, APIs, and error messages to unblock itself and must cite what it found in the SUMMARY. Cost note (fact): search-enabled calls cost more per request on all three, so it's off by default and on only for threads that need it.

R2 built: duck.html is now your chat.html **byte-for-byte**, plus one appended `<style>` + `<script>` (nothing existing edited, no handlers removed). What the additive layer does: per-side edge **nubs** (auto-labeled "Keyboard" in that side's selected language via MyMemory, with cached fallback); tap nub → that side's keyboard slides out (South at bottom normal, North at top rotated 180° so it faces its user; transform-only 180ms slide, zero layout thrash); **Enter** (on-screen key or hardware) commits via the *original* handleSubmit, collapses your keyboard, and slides out the other side's — the baseline's own translation/render/TTS pipeline then runs untouched; typing your nub while the other side owns the keyboard sends them a **localized request** ("The other person would like the keyboard." in *their* language) that resolves by their nub-tap or their Enter, and expires quietly after 10s; a central state machine guarantees only one keyboard is ever open, and the local textarea was made read-only so the OS keyboard never appears. All state events (open/close/handoff/request/timeout, missing-layout warnings) flow into an in-app diagnostics drawer behind a small ⌁ button. One note: I hand-rolled the key layouts (en/zh/km/id/ja/ko/lo/ms/th/vi + default-13 set) instead of inlining Simple Keyboard, since its minified source wasn't provided — flagged in the ledger for possible R3 swap; kana/IME-style composition for Japanese is the known interim limitation. One question: should the request-nub label stay text, or switch to a 🔔 icon so the rotation never renders upside-down text?
